info.title: ClyCites Kernel
info.description: Every application reaches the kernel through this contract and never past it. Records are appended, never changed: a correction is a new record that supersedes the one before it, and a retraction hides a record from default reads without removing it.

post.description: Idempotent on the client-generated id: resubmitting an identical record returns 200 and writes nothing. Reusing an id for different contents is a conflict.

200.description: Already in the log; nothing was written.

409.description: That id belongs to a different record.

422.description: The record is not one the schema allows.

get.description: Superseded and retracted records are absent. Both remain addressable by id.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: A party or entity the record is about — either side of a delivery, either side of a delegation.

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.description: The lawful basis for the read, under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019. Purpose-bound consent is not implemented yet, so naming a purpose is refused.

parameters.name: x-clycites-subject

post.description: Idempotent. Re-registering the same device to the same party returns 200; claiming a device id already held by another party is a conflict.

409.description: That device belongs to another party.

422.description: The registration is not well formed.

post.description: Every record is processed independently, so one bad record does not strand the rest of a device’s outbox. The response is always 200 when the batch itself was well formed; per-record outcomes are in the body. Replaying a batch is safe.

200.description: The batch was received. See each result.

422.description: The batch itself is not well formed.

get.summary: Pull everything appended since a cursor
get.description: The replication feed, oldest first, scoped to the records the requesting party asserted. Unlike a default read it includes superseded and retracted records, because a device holding a partial copy of the log has to be able to resolve a chain without asking. The cursor is held by the device; the kernel keeps no per-device position.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Omit to start from the beginning of the log.

get.description: Checks that the log is reachable.

Normalized mass grouped by the basis of the conversion behind it, and the share of it resting on an unverified default factor. A high assumed share is the honest state of the unit registry, not a fault in the endpoint.

500.description: The rollup could not be computed.

Custody.description: How the kernel arrived at `record.custodian`. Present on lots only.

custodian.description: Who holds the lot now, per the transfer chain.

asserted.description: The custodian named when the lot was created. Kept so the derived answer never erases the claimed one.

as_of.description: When the current holder took it. Null if nothing moved.

broken.description: A transfer moved the lot from a party who was not holding it. Two simultaneous transfers present this way too. Surfaced, never resolved.

SubjectResolution.description: Whether an observation’s `subject_ref` names anything in the log. Present on observations only. Resolved on every read rather than settled at ingest, because an observation can arrive before its subject and later be about something perfectly real.

actual_type.description: The record type actually found. Null if nothing was.

type_matches.description: Null while unknowable — the subject has not arrived, or the declared type names nothing the log can hold. False is permanent and also carries a `subject_type_mismatch` quality flag.

retracted.description: The subject was retracted. Surfaced rather than hiding the observation, which remains someone’s account of what they saw.

BalanceLeg.description: One hand-over, and what the lot weighed when it happened.

expected_kg.description: What it weighed at the previous hand-over, less losses declared since.

discrepancy_kg.description: Positive means mass went missing. Negative means mass appeared, which is no less interesting.

Balance.description: Spec §9.1. Where the lot's mass went, reconciled across the custody sequence — every transfer re-weighs the lot, so the sequence is a series of independent measurements of the same produce. Present on lots only. A discrepancy is always stored and served, never a reason to refuse a record.

declared_loss_kg.description: Sum of `loss.declared` Observations against this lot. Losses are events with an author and a time, not fields on the lot.

tolerance.description: The fraction of the opening weight in force when this was computed. Configurable; the default is a placeholder pending field validation.

breached.description: The whole-lot ratio was exceeded, or any single leg was. A lot that loses 8% and gains it back nets to zero and is still not clean.

incomplete.description: A weighing or a loss could not be read in kilograms, so the arithmetic is partial. A clean-looking balance on an incomplete ledger means nothing.

Fulfilment.description: What the deliveries pointing at this agreement add up to. Present on agreements only. Summed on every read — the agreement stores no counter, because a stored total is wrong the moment a delivery is corrected or retracted.

deliveries.description: Deliveries counted. Superseded and retracted ones are excluded.

confirmed.description: Of those, how many the counterparty confirmed. Arrival and agreement are different facts.

unconvertible.description: Deliveries whose quantity never reached kilograms.

committed_kg.description: Null when the agreement itself was never normalized, in which case the shortfall is unknowable rather than zero.

outstanding_kg.description: Negative when more arrived than was committed. Not clamped: an over-delivery is a fact worth seeing.

incomplete.description: At least one delivery is unconvertible, so `delivered_kg` is a floor and not a total. Any percentage taken from it understates.

quality_flags.description: Kernel-derived labels. Never merged into the record itself, so the asserted body reads back byte for byte. The two exceptions are the fields the schema itself marks derived — `superseded_by` and, on a lot, `custodian` — which the kernel computes rather than serving a stale claim.

superseded_by.description: Direct corrections of this record. More than one entry is a fork: two parties corrected the same record and the kernel will not choose between them.

records.description: Every version of the record, oldest first.

device_id.description: Generated on the device. The kernel never issues one.

results.description: One entry per submitted record, in the order they were sent.
